newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Briton freed but still faces Romania baby trial.
newsitem.headline: Briton freed but still faces Romania baby trial.

text.p: A Briton accused of smuggling one baby out of Romania and of complicity in the illegal adoption of another has been freed from custody pending trial, officials said on Wednesday.
"John Boast was freed from police custody on October 4," a duty officer with the organised crime brigade in the northwestern town of Oradea said by telephone.
"He is subject to judicial control. That means he is not allowed to leave the country and his passport is stamped accordingly."
Boast, 46, a self-described charity worker from Great Harwood in Lancashire, was initially charged in February with smuggling a 15-month-old Gypsy girl out of the country to Britain.
He remained outside custody but was detained in May and charged in a second case -- the purchase for $60 of a two-year-old girl who was also taken out of Romania.
A court in Oradea will continue its hearing into the case on Friday. If convicted, Boast faces up to eight years in prison.
Boast periodically brought truckloads of aid for abandoned children in Romania after the 1989 revolution which toppled dictator Nicolae Ceausescu.

Thousands of babies were taken -- legally and illegally -- from gruesome orphanages in the aftermath of the revolution. But authorities have launched a campaign to rid Romania of its image as an easy source of children for childless Westerners.

A British couple, Adrian and Bernadette Mooney, were convicted in 1994 of trying to smuggle out a baby girl in their car. Their two-year jail sentence was suspended after President Ion Iliescu intervened.
